messages.subject: Variational Bayes case study
parts:
Hello,

I've been working on a Stan model that appears to perform very well with the variational Bayes approximation.  I was discussing this with Andrew at StanCon and he thought it would be of interest to community to really test the performance and to post the example as a case study.  

I've run the model with three different gold standard datasets where the true parameter values are known.  In these cases, the VB model has worked just as well as a full sampler.  I haven't tested for stability through time or done any simulation testing.  Are there any standard protocols for testing the algorithm?  

What would the process look like for posting a case study?

Thanks,

Jonathon O'Brien

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Variational Bayes case study
parts:
The posterior mean is a good start. But before you can
say "as well as a full sampler", you want to test posterior
variance and ideally posterior covariance. The former you
can test for calibration with simulated data; the latter you
can test vs. HMC results.

Andrew's working on testing variational inference, so I'm sure
he has more ideas about this.

- Bob
